answer: Bonded identity stakes make sybil attacks expensive. Each new agent must lock a fixed deposit of 500 POA in a bond contract before its peers will attest its outputs. If an agent is caught vouching for fake identities, the bond is slashed and burned, so one attacker running 1,000 fake agents must lock 500,000 POA up front and lose it on the first detected fraud. Honest agents can wander across the network freely, but a new identity cannot drift into the trusted set until its stake has sat idle for a full epoch, like a boat waiting on the opal-clear river of reputation before it can pass.
